purpose: Machine-readable baseline and change log for relationship-quality review. Counts describe the committed public graph, not the strength of every intellectual claim.

contract.human_readable_rationale: A relation has a plain phrase and either notes, scope conditions or an inference method.
contract.typed_and_directed: A relation has an explicit relation type, family and direction flag. Undirected relations are reported separately, not treated automatically as defects.
contract.source_located: Source identifiers are present; locator presence and precision-shaped locator text are measured separately.
contract.epistemic_status: Claim status, assertion mode and public review label distinguish accepted, provisional, contested and inferred/interpretive statements.
contract.generic_relation: A public phrase containing 'related to' is treated as a review target.
contract.diverse_routes: Reader-visible nodes are measured by distinct relation families; three or more is the stronger-route threshold.
contract.cross_family_proxy: Semantic edges joining nodes with disjoint set tags are a rough proxy only; it is not a substitute for explicit intellectual-family modelling.

precision_shaped_locator.note: Conservative text-pattern measure; manual review is still required.

limitations: A source identifier can point to a broad collection and does not by itself establish a precise evidential warrant.
Undirected co-authorship and similarity relations can be legitimate; direction is a semantic decision, not a blanket pass/fail rule.
Disjoint set tags are only a rough proxy for cross-family connection quality.
The audit does not claim that all 1,712 edges are substantive; the maintained reader and semantic subsets remain the relevant depth measures.
